claim: Visitor, grocery list, individual shopper and extra-purchase temptation are original illustrative framing, not a documented customer's diary.
limit: No invented transaction price, queue length, staffing count or personal testimony.

claim: Saunders established Piggly Wiggly in Memphis in September1916; his self-serving-store patent was filed1916and granted1917.
locator: Patent cover; launch ads; institutional histories
limit: No precise opening-day assertion, worldwide invention priority or sudden universal switch.

claim: Conventional clerk service involved customers placing orders and staff collecting goods; Saunders proposed customers selecting goods themselves.
locator: Patent opening purpose; second advertisement; company history
limit: A common contrast, not every store/one available product or universally lazy clerks.

claim: Patent has front lobby, middle sales room, rear stockroom and alternating aisle connections producing one continuous circuit.
limit: Design reconstruction, not a measured plan of every actual shop. No hidden shortcut in illustration.

claim: A basket station and one-direction entrance gate lead into the circuit; baskets carry selected goods and are returned before departure.
limit: Not trolley or self-checkout; use a hand basket, never depict its permanent removal as standard.

claim: The patent explicitly intends shoppers to review the assortment and become acquainted with different lines of goods while following the route.
limit: Intended exposure, not proof every shopper bought extras or exact uplift.

claim: Goods are packaged for convenient handling; launch ad gives a5lbsugar cloth bag and says articles ready-packed for sale.
locator: Descriptionp1 packages; second ad middle paragraphs
limit: Illustrative advertised example, no sale price, exact brands or barcode. Five-pound bag not modern plastic.

claim: The patent includes a glazed refrigerated cabinet near front middle shelving, paired narrow self-closing doors and visibility from lobby/street through a screened opening.
limit: A proposed cabinet, not present-day wall refrigerators; no claim about refrigerant, electric compressor or exact temperature.

claim: Rear stockroom access, galleries above display cabinets, guardrails and a possible floor-walker are specified to guide customers and monitor stock/sales.
limit: Proposed design feature, not proof of a named employee spying on every shopper in every shop.

claim: The checking station includes basket rests; staff remove goods, check/bill/wrap them, take payment and record the sale before exit.
limit: No barcode, conveyor or unmanned checkout; adding machine and cash register distinct in drawing.

claim: The patent seeks lower overhead and fewer order-fetching clerks; Saunders claims improved margins/capacity but those are his assertions.
limit: No independently certified savings percent, no asserted mass firing, no universal net effect on all labour.

claim: The1916launch advertisement promises no free or paid delivery and jokes that each customer will be her own clerk.
locator: Second ad, own-clerk and no-delivery paragraphs
limit: Attribute to launch offer, not all self-service stores for all time. Do not invent credit policy.

claim: The other launch ad warns against sightseers/timekillers and tells visitors to mean business.
limit: Promotional voice, not authenticated store ban enforced against our Visitor. No invented spoken Saunders quote.

claim: Self-selection redistributes fetching and carrying while staff still stock/check/wrap/take payment; convenience and work can shift together.
limit: Not an allegation that customers became employees or no shop workers remained.

claim: The corporate and museum histories describe franchising the Piggly Wiggly system to other stores.
locator: Corporate history franchise paragraph; museum franchise explanation
limit: No exact count/yeargrowth, no all modern supermarkets descend solely from this one inventor.

claim: A guided route exposes shoppers to more goods than a direct pick-up; an extra item in the Visitor's fictional basket illustrates a possibility, not measured behaviour.
limit: No psychological manipulation metric or guarantee; distinguish planned list from imagined extra.
